import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/training_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/training_4.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']

# Operation 1: JOIN Source4_33_0 and Source4_33_1 on 'batsman'
join_01 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="batsman", how="inner", suffixes=('_0', '_1'))

# Operation 2: JOIN Source4_33_4 and Source4_33_2 on 'batsman'
join_42 = pd.merge(df4, df2, on="batsman", how="inner", suffixes=('_4', '_2'))

# Operation 3: JOIN Source4_33_3 and Source4_33_1 on 'batsman'
join_31 = pd.merge(df3, df1, on="batsman", how="inner", suffixes=('_3', '_1'))

# Operation 4: GROUP BY Source4_33_0.batsman with aggregations:
# avg(Source4_33_0.batsman_runs),
# sum(Source4_33_1.total_runs),
# sum(Source4_33_2.total_runs),
# avg(Source4_33_3.batsman_runs),
# avg(Source4_33_4.batsman_runs)

# To do this, we need to combine all relevant data into one DataFrame keyed by 'batsman'.
# We already have partial joins, but the group by is on Source4_33_0.batsman.
# We will join all source tables on 'batsman' to get all columns aligned for aggregation.

# Merge all sources on 'batsman' starting from df0 (Source4_33_0)
# We will do left joins to keep all batsmen from df0 (since group by is on df0.batsman)
df_01 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="batsman", how="left", suffixes=('_0', '_1'))
df_012 = pd.merge(df_01, df2, on="batsman", how="left", suffixes=('', '_2'))
df_0123 = pd.merge(df_012, df3, on="batsman", how="left", suffixes=('', '_3'))
df_all = pd.merge(df_0123, df4, on="batsman", how="left", suffixes=('', '_4'))

# Now df_all columns:
# batsman
# batsman_runs (from df0)
# total_runs (from df1)
# total_runs_2 (from df2)
# batsman_runs_3 (from df3)
# batsman_runs_4 (from df4)

# Rename columns for clarity before aggregation
df_all.rename(columns={
    'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_0',
    'total_runs': 'total_runs_1',
    'total_runs_2': 'total_runs_2',
    'batsman_runs_3': 'batsman_runs_3',
    'batsman_runs_4': 'batsman_runs_4'
}, inplace=True)

# Perform aggregations grouped by 'batsman' (which is Source4_33_0.batsman)
agg_df = df_all.groupby('batsman', as_index=False).agg({
    'batsman_runs_0': 'mean',   # avg(Source4_33_0.batsman_runs)
    'total_runs_1': 'sum',      # sum(Source4_33_1.total_runs)
    'total_runs_2': 'sum',      # sum(Source4_33_2.total_runs)
    'batsman_runs_3': 'mean',   # avg(Source4_33_3.batsman_runs)
    'batsman_runs_4': 'mean'    # avg(Source4_33_4.batsman_runs)
})

# According to target schema:
# ['batsman': string,
#  'batsman_runs_x': float,
#  'total_runs_x': integer,
#  'total_runs_y': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_y': integer,
#  'batsman_runs': integer]

# Map aggregated columns to target columns:
# batsman_runs_x  <- avg(Source4_33_0.batsman_runs)  => batsman_runs_0 (float)
# total_runs_x    <- sum(Source4_33_1.total_runs)    => total_runs_1 (int)
# total_runs_y    <- sum(Source4_33_2.total_runs)    => total_runs_2 (int)
# batsman_runs_y  <- avg(Source4_33_3.batsman_runs)  => batsman_runs_3 (float)
# batsman_runs    <- avg(Source4_33_4.batsman_runs)  => batsman_runs_4 (float)

# Convert sums to integer as target schema expects integer for total_runs_x and total_runs_y
agg_df['total_runs_1'] = agg_df['total_runs_1'].fillna(0).astype(int)
agg_df['total_runs_2'] = agg_df['total_runs_2'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# For averages, fill NaN with 0.0 (assuming no data means 0)
agg_df['batsman_runs_0'] = agg_df['batsman_runs_0'].fillna(0.0)
agg_df['batsman_runs_3'] = agg_df['batsman_runs_3'].fillna(0.0)
agg_df['batsman_runs_4'] = agg_df['batsman_runs_4'].fillna(0.0)

# The target schema expects batsman_runs_y and batsman_runs as integer,
# but averages are float. The target examples show batsman_runs_y and batsman_runs as integer.
# So we round these averages to nearest integer.
agg_df['batsman_runs_y'] = agg_df['batsman_runs_3'].round().astype(int)
agg_df['batsman_runs'] = agg_df['batsman_runs_4'].round().astype(int)

# Rename columns to target names
agg_df.rename(columns={
    'batsman_runs_0': 'batsman_runs_x',
    'total_runs_1': 'total_runs_x',
    'total_runs_2': 'total_runs_y',
}, inplace=True)

# Select and order columns as per target schema
target_df = agg_df[['batsman', 'batsman_runs_x', 'total_runs_x', 'total_runs_y', 'batsman_runs_y', 'batsman_runs']]

# Save to target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/target_multisource.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
